svg.title: PoisonedRefresh kill chain - F5 BIG-IP APM rootkit with a memory-only PHP web shell
svg.desc: Two-lane kill chain. Left lane, the BIG-IP APM appliance: 1 an exposed APM virtual server with an access policy, 2 unauthenticated remote code execution through CVE-2025-53521, which is on the CISA KEV list, 3 an installer named umount that runs as root, weakens SELinux and prepends an implant to /usr/sbin/httpd, 4 persistence inside BIG-IP install images, 5 a second stage that hooks the Apache start-up and hides strings with RC4, 6 a web shell injected into memory for three webtop PHP scripts while the files on disk stay unchanged, 7 a local UNIX socket at /run/bigtlog.pipe that binds a bash shell. Right lane, the operator and the defenders: A reconnaissance against the device-info REST endpoint, B the entry and delivery steps that are not public, C web shell tasking by HTTP POST answered with 201 and a CSS content type, D three vendor names for one implant, E no attribution, F the defender response of memory capture, F5 checks and rebuild. Critical stages are shown in red.
svg.text: PoisonedRefresh: a memory-only web shell inside F5 BIG-IP APM
Vendor: Sophos X-Ops + ESET + F5 - Date: 2026-09-09 - Cluster: F5 activity c05d5254 (unattributed) - Day 112
BIG-IP APM APPLIANCE (what defenders see)
OPERATOR AND DEFENDER VIEW (what is public)
Exposed APM virtual server with an access policy
Condition for CVE-2025-53521: APM policy on a virtual server
T1190 Exploit Public-Facing Application
Shadowserver: 795 exposed endpoints (2026-09-07)
Unauthenticated RCE: CVE-2025-53521 (on KEV)
Published 2025-10-15 as DoS; reclassified RCE 9.8 on 2026-03-27
Exploited in the wild; KEV added 2026-03-27, due 2026-03-30
How the installer reaches the box is not public
T1190 CWE-121 stack-based buffer overflow
F5 K000156741 advisory, K000160486 IOCs
Installer 'umount' runs as root and weakens SELinux
Prepends a 0x5430-byte implant to /usr/sbin/httpd
Infects umount, httpd and rc.local inside install images
SELinux disabled or httpd_t mount_t apd_t made permissive
path /mnt/tm_install/
Persistence across upgrades
Install-image copies are rewritten, so an upgrade can re-seed
Sophos and ESET describe it; no advisory says a fix removes it
A restart removes only the running copy
T1554 Compromise Host Software Binary
sys-eicheck fails when umount or httpd changed
Stage 2 hooks the Apache start-up
Own ELF loader reads /proc/self/exe; RC4 hides the strings
__libc_start_main wrapper runs before main() in each worker
apr_dso_load hook waits until libphp is loaded
T1027 T1014 RC4 key TrswBWIl90Z5e38n
SHA256 26bd5b0722d1dbab...d57bccc9
Memory-only web shell in three webtop scripts
Patches open, close, mmap in libphp via /proc/self/maps
apm_css.php3, full_wt.php3, webtop_popup_css.php3 get the shell
prepended when PHP maps them; files on disk are unchanged
POST body prefix BSOHAzPB then eval()
Local socket /run/bigtlog.pipe binds /bin/bash
Started by an apr_time_now trigger after server start-up
Token Kzwd6jM5; no TCP listener; fork() for more sessions
Sophos found no client component for the socket
T1059.004 Unix Shell
ls -l /run/bigtlog.pipe /run/bigstart.ltm
A
Fingerprinting of exposed devices
Defused honeypots saw requests for the device-info REST path
/mgmt/shared/identified-devices/config/device-info
Returns hostname and machine ID; seen after 2026-03-27
Suricata sid 6290004, KQL k2
B
Entry and delivery: the part that is not public
Exploit request and the way umount lands are not described
F5 lists bash through iControl REST from localhost, with a
base64 string echoed to a file and run as bigstart.ltm
restjavad-audit auditd audit logs
KQL k1 correlates two signal classes
C
Three names for one implant
F5 tracks activity c05d5254 and published IOCs in March
ESET analysed related samples in April: PoisonedRefresh
Sophos detection Linux/Agnt-IC; analysis dated 7 September
single Sophos sample, SHA256 only
ESET SHA1s relayed by a secondary summary
D
Attribution: none
Sophos: not enough evidence to name an actor
ESET had not settled attribution (per The Hacker News)
No victim named and no victim count published
confidence: high (family), none (actor)
edge-device focus is not attribution
E
Web shell tasking over HTTP
POST to a webtop script; body is BSOHAzPB plus encrypted code
Stream cipher key wSLjN1beuR, payload run with eval()
Answer: HTTP 201, Content-Type text/css; charset=utf-8
Suricata sids 6290001-6290003
Sigma 03: webserver 201 plus script name
F
Defender response
Patching is necessary but does not prove a clean device
Capture memory and a qkview, run sys-eicheck, open an F5 case
If unsure, rebuild from known-good media and rotate secrets
UK NCSC: investigate whenever the update was applied
Sigma 01-04, YARA x3, PEAK H1-H3
Detection anchors: /run/bigtlog.pipe, /run/bigstart.ltm, BSOHAzPB body prefix, 201 text/css, httpd and umount integrity
Rules in this folder: Sigma 01-04, KQL k1-k2, YARA poisonedrefresh_f5_bigip.yar (3 rules), Suricata sids 6290001-6290004, PEAK hunts H1-H3.
The web shell lives only in memory: file integrity monitoring on the three .php3 scripts is blind, so compare memory with disk and run sys-eicheck.
No network indicators were published; hashes are one SHA256 from Sophos and two SHA1 relayed from ESET (medium confidence).
